title: Vector triangles for coplanar equilibrium mark scheme

questions.answer: The resultant force is zero and the resultant moment or torque about any point is zero.
accepted_alternatives: The vector sum of the forces is zero and the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about any point.

marking_points.text: States that the resultant force in any direction is zero
States that the resultant moment or torque about any point is zero

option_feedback.A: A common tail is useful for a force diagram, but equal arrow lengths do not make the vector sum zero.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Returning to the first tail after head-to-tail addition means the resultant vector is zero.
option_feedback.C: Parallel and perpendicular directions alone do not ensure that the vector sum is zero.
option_feedback.D: Force magnitudes are positive numbers. Their directions must be included in the vector sum.

marking_points.text: Selects B, identifying a closed head-to-tail force polygon as zero resultant force

option_feedback.A: Reversing an arrow changes the direction of that force and therefore changes the vector represented.
option_feedback.B: Rotating an arrow changes the force direction and is not a valid rearrangement.
option_feedback.C: Correct. The same directed arrows may be placed in another cyclic order and still form the same closed sum.
option_feedback.D: Changing a side length changes the force magnitude at the chosen scale.

marking_points.text: Selects C, preserving every force magnitude and direction while changing only the cyclic order

option_feedback.A: Correct. Closure establishes force balance, while an extended body needs a separate torque check.
option_feedback.B: The same force vectors can act on different lines of action, so closure alone does not establish zero torque.
option_feedback.C: Zero resultant force is also consistent with motion at constant velocity.
option_feedback.D: A closed triangle can have three unequal side lengths.

marking_points.text: Selects A, distinguishing zero resultant force from the separate zero-torque condition

questions.answer: The 36 N east and 48 N north arrows are followed by P back to the start. P is 60 N at 53.1 degrees south of west.
accepted_alternatives: 60 N at 36.9 degrees west of south
questions.unit_policy: Units are required for force magnitudes. An unambiguous compass direction is required for the angle.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A 3.0 cm arrow east followed by a 4.0 cm arrow north, then a labelled arrow P from the final head back to the original tail.
accepted_alternatives: Any cyclic reorder of the same three correctly directed and scaled arrows.
parts.unit_policy: The stated scale must be used consistently.

marking_points.text: Draws the 36 N and 48 N forces as 3.0 cm and 4.0 cm arrows in the correct east and north directions, placed head-to-tail
Draws and labels P as the closing arrow from the final head back to the original tail

parts.label: (b)
parts.unit_policy: Accept 60 N or a scale measurement consistent with the drawing within 0.5 N.

marking_points.text: Uses the right-angled force triangle to obtain P = 60 N

parts.label: (c)
parts.unit_policy: The angle and quadrant must both be correct.

marking_points.text: Uses tan theta = 48/36 for the acute angle measured from west
Obtains a direction of 53.1 degrees south of west for P

questions.answer: A plus B has components 10.0 N east and 69.3 N north, so C is 70.0 N at 8.21 degrees west of south.
accepted_alternatives: C has components 10.0 N west and 69.3 N south.
questions.unit_policy: Units and directions are required for every component and final force.

parts.label: (a)
accepted_alternatives: +10.0 N horizontally and +69.3 N vertically when east and north are positive
parts.unit_policy: Both component values must include unambiguous signs or directions.

marking_points.text: Calculates the horizontal component of A plus B as 50 - 80 cos 60 degrees = 10.0 N east
Calculates the vertical component of A plus B as 80 sin 60 degrees = 69.3 N north

parts.label: (b)
parts.unit_policy: The final magnitude must be stated in N.

marking_points.text: Recognises that C has components 10.0 N west and 69.3 N south to close the force triangle
Calculates C = sqrt(10.0 squared + 69.3 squared) = 70.0 N

parts.label: (c)
parts.unit_policy: The angle and quadrant must both be correct.

marking_points.text: Uses tan theta = 10.0/69.3 for the acute angle measured from south
Obtains a direction of 8.21 degrees west of south for C

questions.answer: The cable tension is 240 N. The weight, tension and hinge reaction form a closed triangle. R is 240 N at 30.0 degrees above the horizontal towards the right.
accepted_alternatives: The hinge force has components 208 N right and 120 N up.
questions.unit_policy: Force values require N and the reaction direction must be unambiguous.

parts.label: (a)
parts.unit_policy: The tension must be stated in N.

marking_points.text: Forms the clockwise weight moment about the hinge as 240 x 0.60 N m
Equates moments using (T sin 30 degrees) x 1.2 = 240 x 0.60
Obtains T = 240 N

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: A closed head-to-tail triangle containing the 240 N downward weight, the 240 N tension at 30 degrees above the horizontal towards the wall, and R as the correctly directed closing side.
accepted_alternatives: Any cyclic reorder preserving all three vector directions and magnitudes.
parts.unit_policy: Force labels and arrow directions are required.

marking_points.text: Draws the weight and cable tension with their correct directions and places the three force arrows head-to-tail
Draws and labels R as the closing side so that the vector triangle returns to its starting point

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: 240 N at 30.0 degrees above the horizontal towards the right
accepted_alternatives: 240 N at 60.0 degrees to the upward vertical towards the right
parts.unit_policy: Accept an equivalent angle only with the correct upward and rightward quadrant.

marking_points.text: Obtains hinge-reaction components of 240 cos 30 degrees = 208 N right and 240 - 240 sin 30 degrees = 120 N up
Calculates the hinge-reaction magnitude as 240 N
Gives the hinge-reaction direction as 30.0 degrees above the horizontal towards the right
